references.text: God promised to bring the people of Israel out of Egypt, which was fulfilled in the exodus described here.
The Lord's promise to Abraham to give the land to his descendants, as referred to by the angel of the Lord.
God's oath to Isaac to give the land to his offspring, part of the promise made to the fathers.
God's promise to Jacob concerning the land, which is part of the covenant with the fathers mentioned here.
The angel of the Lord appears in a burning bush, the same divine messenger who speaks at Bokim.
God promises to send His angel ahead of Israel to lead them into the promised land.
Gilgal was the place where Israel camped after crossing the Jordan, the starting point for the angel's journey.
The commander of the Lord's army appears to Joshua, a similar divine manifestation.
God confirms that He kept His promise and brought Israel out of Egypt and into the land.
A warning that the people will break the covenant, contrasting with God's promise never to break His covenant.
